PullRequest.Title: agentHost: report Git stderr and shell tool results when Windows E2E fixtures fail
PullRequest.Body:
Diagnostics only, for two Windows Agent Host E2E failures in main CI (pipeline 727) where the log doesn't contain the actual error. Test-only, with no behavior, timeout or retry changes.

## The two failures

**[499859](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=499859), Claude file tests** (`renames a workspace file`, `creates a file in a new nested directory`):
- Both tests have Claude run one pinned shell command (`node -e "…renameSync…"` / `node -e "…writeFileSync…"`), then check the workspace. The file never changed, so the asserts failed with `true !== false` and `ENOENT`.
- In the Agent Host logs, those two turns are the only Claude turns in either shard that took over 3 s. Both took about 35.9 s and overlapped. The host log doesn't record what the shell tool returned.

**[499974](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=499974), Conformance** (`branch completions ignore unmatched search text`):
- `initTestGitRepo` threw `Command failed: git init`. `execSync` passes stderr through to the parent process, and in the Electron test runner it doesn't show up in the log, so Git's actual message is lost.

Neither has repeated, and pipeline 700 ran Windows Agent Host E2E clean 20/20 on the same day. Without the error text, the next hit wouldn't tell us anything new either.

## Change

- **`initTestGitRepo` / `disableTestGitMaintenance`:** run their Git commands with stderr piped. On failure they throw `Command failed: <command> (exit N): <stderr, at most 500 characters>`, keeping the original error as `cause`. The commands themselves are unchanged.
- **The two Claude file tests:** if the expected file change is missing, the assertion message lists what the turn's tool calls returned (`success`, `error`, and the first 300 characters of their text result). The pass criteria are unchanged.

None of this logs environment variables or tokens. It's only Git's stderr and the tool's own result text.

## Validation

- `tsc` has no errors in the changed files, and `oxlint` is clean.
- I checked the error shape with the same `execSync` options: `git config` outside a repo gives `Command failed: git config user.name x (exit 128): fatal: not in a git directory`.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize ordinary or bare Git test fixtures and disable maintenance in clones.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture setup must finish before the test creates sessions or exercises Git-backed features. Each synchronous Git command blocks setup until completion, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute git init and local identity/maintenance configuration commands; these subprocesses also access the fixture filesystem.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five sequential shell/Git executions per initialized repository, including bare repositories; two per explicit disableTestGitMaintenance call on a clone. Representative remote-workspace helpers initialize two repositories, with unchanged counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same execSync commands ran in the same order and at the same frequency. The wrapper changes stdin/stderr handling, not subprocess count or placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All commands remain synchronous prerequisites for the fixture's test.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicitly created test repositories and clones, not branch count, files, or notification count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Commands serialize within the test worker because execSync blocks. No new parallel execution, retries, or background maintenance is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache, negative cache, or coalescing involved. New test directories are initialized independently; warm OS/Git caches do not alter call counts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete hunk preserves each command, ordering, and maintenance setting; representative callers and existing fixture tests corroborate fixed call counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual process-start and filesystem durations vary by platform, but those costs are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Piping stderr changes diagnostics for small fixture commands without adding subprocesses or materially increasing successful-path work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A fixture Git command fails during setup.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command must exit before setup throws. The new wrapper then constructs diagnostic text and rethrows with the original error as cause; no later test work can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collect the failed Git command's stderr through a pipe and include a shortened diagnostic in the thrown error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One failed subprocess and one error conversion at the first failing setup command; subsequent commands do not execute.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command already executed synchronously and threw on failure; stderr was passed to the parent by execSync's default handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds in-memory diagnostic formatting after the existing failed command, not another boundary call or retry.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Bytes of stderr from a single git init or git config failure. The displayed detail is capped at 500 characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous command per worker; formatting occurs once after failure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Failures are neither retried nor cached. No new retained collection or persistent cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the failure-only conversion and absence of additional commands; no evidence of a meaningful scaling workload for the added formatting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unusual Git installations could emit more diagnostics, but these fixed init/config commands provide no realistic large-output trigger establishing a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Failure diagnostics do not remove or fix an old performance mechanism, so no regression-fix provenance report applies.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create output/report.txt in a new nested directory through the shell E2E turn.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Create a workspace and session, complete the pinned shell turn and unread transition, perform filesystem assertions, then compare the AHP snapshot. The new diagnostic string is eagerly computed at assertion evaluation even on success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use local WebSocket JSON-RPC for initialization, authentication, session creation, session/chat subscriptions, turn dispatch, and any tool confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five awaited setup requests, one turn dispatch, and confirmations only when requested. The recorded Claude fixture has one tool invocation and two model exchanges. No new RPC is made by describeTurnToolResults.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical session/turn protocol operations and replay/live-provider behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session setup and turn completion remain prerequisites to the assertions; diagnostic formatting reads already-received notifications.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The existing pinned provider shell command runs node to create output and write a small fixed report.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shell tool invocation in the recorded Claude scenario, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The exact same command ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The turn waits for tool completion before the filesystem assertions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check report existence, read its fixed content, and perform the existing snapshot assertion or snapshot-update write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly added existsSync per test run; one existing readFileSync and existing snapshot operation on success. A missing file now stops at the existence assertion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Read the report directly and perform the same snapshot assertion; no explicit existence probe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: One additional metadata lookup occurs after the completed shell turn and before the existing read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One completed turn's notifications and tool-result text. driveTurn clears received notifications before dispatch. The pinned command produces no normal output and the Claude recording contains one completion, not a suite-wide history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Setup RPCs and the single turn are awaited sequentially. The notification scan and assertion formatting run synchronously once; no fan-out or new parallel tasks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The summary uses existing in-memory notifications and performs no resource reads or network fetches. Notification history is cleared per driven turn; workspace files are fresh per test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced driveTurn clearing, receivedNotifications filtering, both assertion arguments, and the complete 39-line Claude capture.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Live-provider failures may produce more result text than replay, but no concrete large-output workload is established for this fixed silent command.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Eager summary generation and one extra filesystem existence check are real additions, but their fixed small test workload does not establish a material performance issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rename before.txt to after.txt through the shell E2E turn.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Create workspace and seed file, establish the session, complete the pinned rename turn and unread transition, assert source disappearance and destination content, then compare the existing snapshot. Tool-result formatting is evaluated once as the source assertion's message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize/authenticate/create/subscribe over local WebSocket JSON-RPC, dispatch the turn, and answer any tool-confirmation notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five setup requests and one turn dispatch plus required confirmations. Recorded Claude replay has two model exchanges and one shell completion. Added diagnostics make zero RPC calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setup, dispatch, confirmation, and completion behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing protocol and tool completion waits precede assertions, with unchanged ordering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the unchanged pinned node renameSync command through the provider shell tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shell tool invocation in the recorded Claude fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical pinned shell command and tool invocation count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rename tool completion remains part of the existing turn completion wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the fixed seed file, probe source existence, read destination content, and compare or update the AHP snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One seed write, one existing existsSync, one existing readFileSync, and the existing snapshot operation per successful test; none added by this rename-test hunk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same filesystem operations and snapshot assertion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Seed setup precedes the turn; existing reads/assertions follow it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The completed single turn's notifications and completion text, rather than all prior suite turns. The recorded rename command completes with no output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single awaited turn and synchronous once-per-test formatting. No additional subprocess, request, queue, retry, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Notification history is reset by driveTurn; describeTurnToolResults filters existing memory without creating a cache or extending notification ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after assertion comparison and the recorded tool result establish unchanged boundary counts and a small diagnostic-only addition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional live failure diagnostics could be larger, but there is no realistic high-volume output trigger in this fixed rename scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The new eager summary is bounded by the current small turn in this scenario, not an accumulating history or hot production path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the entire two-file inventory and both complete diff pages. Traced fixture callers, notification ownership/reset, turn completion, WebSocket serialization, fixed shell captures, and snapshot/filesystem boundaries. No actionable high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix found. Static review only.
